# `tailwind/no-unknown-classes`

**Every class is one the project's Tailwind knows**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Pack** | `@codelaw/rules-tailwind` (npm) · `codelaw-rules-tailwind` (PyPI) |
| **Languages** | JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX, HTML |
| **Turned on by** | `codelaw:tailwind/recommended` at `warn` |
| **Severity when named without one** | `error` |
| **Options** | `ignore` |
| **Fix** | `suggest` — `codelaw fix --unsafe` applies it; review the diff, it can change behaviour (an unknown class may be styled by the project's own CSS or read by a script; removing it needs a person) |
| **Stability** | `preview` — runs only with `preview = true` |
| **Since** | 0.5.0 |
| **Ported from** | `eslint-plugin-better-tailwindcss/no-unknown-classes` |

## What it checks

Every class in a class list is one the project's own Tailwind CSS generates, its theme and plugins included, as `@codelaw/provider-tailwind` reports. Name the project's own classes in `ignore`.

**Why:** A typo (`fleex`) or a class from another version silently styles nothing.

It reads the class table `@codelaw/provider-tailwind` builds from the project's own `tailwindcss`; without the table it finds nothing, and the run says why (`[providers] on_missing`).

## Configuration

Everything below goes in `codelaw.toml` at the repo root. The same keys work as `[tool.codelaw]` in `pyproject.toml` or `"codelaw"` in `package.json` ([SR-CONFIG](../../../records/0110_config.md)).

### Turn it on

**Install the pack** (`codelaw init` does it for the languages it finds):

```bash
npm install --save-dev @codelaw/rules-tailwind
pip install codelaw-rules-tailwind
```

**Then extend a preset that turns it on** — `codelaw:tailwind/recommended` sets it to `warn`:

```toml
preview = true                        # pack rules are preview today
extends = ["codelaw:tailwind/recommended"]
```

- **A rule exists only once its pack is loaded** through `extends`; naming it in `[rules]` without that is an unknown rule id (exit 2).
- **Without `preview = true`** the rule is skipped and codelaw warns that it is preview.

### Severity

```toml
[rules]
"tailwind/no-unknown-classes" = "warn"    # error | warn | info | off
```

- **`error`** fails the run (exit 1) · **`warn`** fails only with `--max-warnings N` · **`info`** never fails · **`off`** turns it off.
- **Naming it with a severity turns it on** even when no preset does.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ignore` | `string[]` | `[]` | regular expressions for the project's own classes, each matched against a whole class |

**Every option at its default** — a starting point to copy:

```toml
[rules."tailwind/no-unknown-classes"]
severity = "error"

[rules."tailwind/no-unknown-classes".options]
ignore = []
```

**The same, inline, with example values:**

```toml
[rules]
"tailwind/no-unknown-classes" = { severity = "error", options = { ignore = ["<name>"] } }
```

- **A table without `severity`** changes only the options: the severity stays what a preset or an earlier layer set, and a rule that is off stays off.
- **A list option replaces its default** — copy the default entries you want to keep.
- **An unknown option or a value of the wrong type** stops the run with exit 2 and names the nearest option.

#### `ignore`

*string[]* · default `[]`

regular expressions for the project's own classes, each matched against a whole class

```toml
[rules."tailwind/no-unknown-classes".options]
ignore = ["<name>"]
```

### For a group of files

A `[scope.<name>]` gives some files their own setting, applied after `[rules]` — the `tests` scope `codelaw:js/recommended` ships (`**/*.test.*`, `**/*.spec.*`); naming it extends it, so its files stay:

```toml
[scope.tests]
rules = { "tailwind/no-unknown-classes" = { options = { ignore = ["<name>"] } } }
```

Or switch it off there:

```toml
[scope.tests]
rules = { "tailwind/no-unknown-classes" = "off" }
```

A scope's `remap` changes whole severities in its files, after everything else: `remap = { error = "warn" }` never fails the run there.

### Warn locally, fail in CI

The `ci` profile runs when `CI` is set; `local` otherwise; `--profile <name>` or `CODELAW_PROFILE` picks one.

```toml
[profile.local.rules]
"tailwind/no-unknown-classes" = "warn"

[profile.ci.rules]
"tailwind/no-unknown-classes" = "error"
```

### In `pyproject.toml` or `package.json`

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[tool.codelaw.rules]
"tailwind/no-unknown-classes" = { severity = "warn", options = { ignore = ["<name>"] } }
```

```json
{
  "codelaw": {
    "rules": {
      "tailwind/no-unknown-classes": {"severity": "warn", "options": {"ignore": ["<name>"]}}
    }
  }
}
```

### Silence one finding

An inline `codelaw-ignore` always needs a reason; `expires=`, `warn_days=` and `by=` date it ([SR-LINTER](../../../records/0106_linter.md) decision 6).

- **JavaScript:** `// codelaw-ignore tailwind/no-unknown-classes: <reason>`
- **HTML:** `<!-- codelaw-ignore tailwind/no-unknown-classes: <reason> -->`
- **Dated:** `// codelaw-ignore tailwind/no-unknown-classes expires=2026-12-31 by=you@example.com: <reason>`

### Keep today's findings, fail on new ones

```bash
codelaw baseline add --rule tailwind/no-unknown-classes --expires 2026-12-31 --reason "<why>"
```

See [SR-BASELINE](../../../records/0104_baseline-and-deprecations.md).

### See what applies

```bash
codelaw explain tailwind/no-unknown-classes       # what it wants, why, how to fix
codelaw check --rule tailwind/no-unknown-classes  # only this rule
codelaw config --print --for <file>               # the resolved setting, and where it came from
```

## How to fix

1. Fix the typo, or remove the class.
2. If the project's CSS defines it, add a pattern for it to `ignore`.

## Examples

### JavaScript

#### Don't

```js
export const box = cn("flex fleex");
```

#### Do

```js
export const box = cn("flex");
```

### JSX

#### Don't

```jsx
export const Box = () => <div className="flex fleex" />;
```

#### Do

```jsx
export const Box = () => <div className="flex" />;
```

### TypeScript

#### Don't

```ts
export const box = cn("flex fleex");
```

#### Do

```ts
export const box = cn("flex");
```

### TSX

#### Don't

```tsx
export const Box = () => <div className="flex fleex" />;
```

#### Do

```tsx
export const Box = () => <div className="flex" />;
```

### HTML

#### Don't

```html
<div class="flex fleex"></div>
```

#### Do

```html
<div class="flex"></div>
```
